sanskrit_verse:
अन्यवादी क्रियाद्वेषी नोपस्थाता निरुत्तरः।
आहूतप्रपलायी च हीनः पञ्चविधः स्मृतः॥
transliteration: anyavādī kriyādveṣī nopasthātā niruttaraḥ | āhūtaprapalāyī ca hīnaḥ pañcavidhaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who speaks against the action of another, one who resists rightful duty, one who fails to appear when summoned, one who flees after being called, and one deficient in capacity—these five are declared as legally incapacitated.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not personal assertion.
Causation is established through conscious participation in dharmic order.
Capacity-based responsibility determines eligibility for legal engagement.
Restoration occurs through realignment with the causal integrity of action.
Consciousness misalignment manifests as incapacity, not inherent fault.
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent opposes a lawful dharmic action → THEN disqualify from legal standing until realignment verified.
IF agent refuses rightful duty without valid cause → THEN suspend legal capacity pending restoration process.
IF agent fails to appear upon lawful summons → THEN classify as non-responsive and defer case until presence assured.
IF agent flees after lawful notice → THEN initiate completion protocol to restore presence and intent.
IF agent lacks cognitive or energetic capacity → THEN apply capacity-building measures before legal inclusion.
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Adjudication, any party demonstrating these five incapacities shall be excluded from active litigation until full restoration of capacity and alignment with Dharma is confirmed by authorized spiritual-legal authority. The Court must prioritize restoration over procedural exclusion.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that misalignment with dharma arises from ignorance or incapacity, not malice. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how failure to engage leads to further disconnection. Responsibility is proportional to consciousness and capacity. Non-punitive rule holds that all beings are capable of restoration when supported by right knowledge and energetic alignment.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Śuddhi Kriya to purify energetic resistance to lawful summons.
Assign Vak Siddhi practice to restore truthful and timely verbal response.
Implement Tapobalika protocol to rebuild diminished capacity through disciplined action.
Engage Guru Yukti process for guided reintegration into lawful societal function.
Apply Dharmic Completion Ritual to resolve fleeing behavior and reaffirm commitment to truth process.
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of Law. This verse is executed as pure Dharma, restoring alignment through consciousness, not punishment. Reality is non-punitive; consciousness is the ultimate judge. Dharma is restored.
